entries.name: print
entries.summary: Writes its arguments to the simulator console (not the screen).
entries.description: Separated by tabs, ending in a newline. On the device it goes to the USB console, which is not always available; draw on the screen with the Screen framework instead.

entries.name: type
entries.summary: The type of a value as a string: "nil", "boolean", "number", "string", "table", "function", "thread" or "userdata".

entries.name: tostring
entries.summary: Converts any value to a string (using __tostring if the metatable has it).

entries.name: tonumber
entries.summary: Converts a string (or number) to a number, or nil when it cannot.
entries.description: With base (2-36) the string is read as an integer in that base.
entries.example:
local n = tonumber(args[1]) or 0
local bits = tonumber("1011", 2)

entries.name: pairs
entries.summary: Iterates every key/value pair of a table, in no particular order.
entries.returns: iterator for `for k, v in pairs(t)`
entries.example: for key, value in pairs(config) do print(key, value) end

entries.name: ipairs
entries.summary: Iterates the array part of a table: t[1], t[2], ... up to the first nil.
entries.returns: iterator for `for i, v in ipairs(t)`
entries.example: for i, line in ipairs(lines) do Screen.OutText(0, i - 1, line) end

entries.name: next
entries.summary: The next key/value after `key` in a table (nil key starts). `next(t) == nil` tests for an empty table.

entries.name: select
entries.summary: The arguments from the n-th onward; select("#", ...) counts them.

entries.name: assert
entries.summary: Raises an error with `message` when v is false or nil; otherwise returns its arguments.
entries.description: Handy with calls that return nil, err: assert(fs.writeall(path, data)).

entries.name: error
entries.summary: Raises an error. level 1 (default) blames the caller of error, 2 the caller's caller.
entries.description: An uncaught error ends the program (finish() still runs) and is written to logs/errors on the card.
entries.example: if not ok then error("cannot load level " .. n) end

entries.name: pcall
entries.summary: Calls f in protected mode: errors are caught instead of ending the program.
entries.returns: true, results... or false, error message
entries.example:
local ok, err = pcall(dofile, "/data/plugin.lua")
if not ok then Screen.OutLine("plugin failed: " .. err) end

entries.name: xpcall
entries.summary: Like pcall, but calls msgh(error) before unwinding, so it can add a traceback.
entries.returns: true, results... or false, msgh's result

entries.name: setmetatable
entries.summary: Gives table t the metatable mt (nil removes it). Returns t.
entries.description: Metatables add behaviour: __index for defaults and methods, __tostring, __eq, arithmetic hooks. The Timer framework's objects use __index.

entries.name: getmetatable
entries.summary: The metatable of a value, or nil.

entries.name: rawget
entries.summary: t[k] without invoking __index.

entries.name: rawset
entries.summary: t[k] = v without invoking __newindex.

entries.name: rawequal
entries.summary: Equality without __eq.

entries.name: rawlen
entries.summary: The length of a table or string without __len.

entries.name: collectgarbage
entries.summary: Controls the garbage collector: "collect" runs a full cycle, "count" returns the heap in KB, "step", "stop", "restart", "incremental", "generational".
entries.description: Programs have a 96 KB heap cap; a full collect between levels keeps the collector from running mid-frame.

entries.name: load
entries.summary: Compiles a string (or reader function) of Lua code into a function without running it.
entries.example:
local f = load("return " .. expr)
local value = f and f()

entries.name: warn
entries.summary: Emits a warning to the console (off unless warn("@on") was called).

entries.name: _G
entries.summary: The table of globals.

entries.name: _VERSION
entries.summary: The Lua version string ("Lua 5.5").

entries.name: local
entries.summary: Declares a variable in the current block (or a function). Locals are faster than globals and stay out of the program's global table.
entries.example:
local x, y = 0, 0
local function step() end

entries.name: function
entries.summary: Defines a function; `function name(...)`, `local function name(...)`, or an anonymous `function(...) end` value.
entries.example:
local function add(a, b)
    return a + b
end

entries.name: if
entries.summary: Conditional: if ... then ... elseif ... then ... else ... end. Only nil and false are false.
entries.example:
if score > best then
    best = score
elseif score == best then
    tie = true
else
    tie = false
end

entries.name: for
entries.summary: Numeric loop `for i = start, stop [, step] do` or generic loop `for k, v in pairs(t) do`. The loop variable is a fresh const local each iteration (Lua 5.5): assign to a copy if you need to change it.
entries.example:
for i = 1, 10 do ... end
for i = 10, 1, -1 do ... end
for _, v in ipairs(list) do ... end

entries.name: while
entries.summary: Loop while a condition holds: while cond do ... end.
entries.example: while n > 0 do n = n - 1 end

entries.name: repeat
entries.summary: Loop that tests at the end: repeat ... until cond (the body's locals are visible in cond).
entries.example:
repeat
    local ev = InputPoll()
until ev == nil

entries.name: break
entries.summary: Leaves the innermost loop.
entries.example: for i, v in ipairs(t) do if v == target then found = i break end end

entries.name: goto
entries.summary: Jumps to a label `::name::` in the same function (useful for `continue`).
entries.example:
for i = 1, 10 do
    if skip(i) then goto continue end
    work(i)
    ::continue::
end

entries.name: return
entries.summary: Returns values from a function; must be the last statement of its block.

entries.name: do
entries.summary: Opens a block: do ... end scopes locals.
entries.example:
do
    local tmp = compute()
    use(tmp)
end

entries.name: and
entries.summary: Logical and: returns the first false/nil operand or the last one. Short-circuits.

entries.name: or
entries.summary: Logical or: returns the first true operand. The idiom for defaults: x = x or 0.

entries.name: not
entries.summary: Logical not: true for nil and false, false otherwise.

entries.name: nil
entries.summary: The absence of a value; a table field set to nil is removed.

entries.name: true
entries.summary: Boolean true.

entries.name: false
entries.summary: Boolean false (only nil and false are falsy; 0 and "" are true).

entries.name: end
entries.summary: Closes a block opened by function, if, for, while or do.

entries.name: then
entries.summary: Follows an if or elseif condition.

entries.name: else
entries.summary: The alternative branch of an if.

entries.name: elseif
entries.summary: Another condition in an if chain.

entries.name: in
entries.summary: Separates the variables from the iterator in a generic for.
entries.example: for k, v in pairs(t) do end

entries.name: until
entries.summary: Ends a repeat loop with its condition.

entries.name: string
entries.summary: String functions; also available as methods on any string (s:upper()).
entries.description: Strings are immutable byte strings: # gives the byte length, indexes count from 1, negative indexes count from the end.

entries.name: string.byte
entries.summary: The byte codes of characters i..j (default the first).

entries.name: string.char
entries.summary: A string from byte codes.

entries.name: string.find
entries.summary: Finds pattern in s; plain = true searches for the literal text.
entries.example:
local i, j = s:find("world")
local k = s:find(".", 1, true) -- a literal dot

entries.name: string.format
entries.summary: C-style formatting: %d %5d %05d %x %f %.2f %s %-10s %q %%.

entries.name: string.gmatch
entries.summary: Iterates every match of pattern in s.
entries.example: for word in line:gmatch("%S+") do table.insert(words, word) end

entries.name: string.gsub
entries.summary: Replaces matches of pattern with repl (a string with %1 captures, a table or a function).

entries.name: string.len
entries.summary: Byte length (same as #s).

entries.name: string.lower
entries.summary: Lower-case copy.

entries.name: string.upper
entries.summary: Upper-case copy.

entries.name: string.match
entries.summary: The captures of the first match of pattern (or the whole match).

entries.name: string.rep
entries.summary: s repeated n times.

entries.name: string.reverse
entries.summary: The bytes in reverse order.

entries.name: string.sub
entries.summary: The substring from i to j (negative counts from the end).
entries.example:
local first = s:sub(1, 1)
local last3 = s:sub(-3)

entries.name: string.pack
entries.summary: Packs values into a binary string (e.g. "<I2" a little-endian 16-bit).

entries.name: string.unpack
entries.summary: Unpacks values from a binary string.

entries.name: string.packsize
entries.summary: The size a pack format produces.

entries.name: table
entries.summary: Table (array) helpers.
entries.description: Tables are the only data structure: arrays (1-based), records, and both at once.

entries.name: table.insert
entries.summary: Appends value (or inserts it at pos, shifting the rest).

entries.name: table.remove
entries.summary: Removes and returns the last element (or the one at pos).

entries.name: table.concat
entries.summary: Joins strings/numbers of an array into one string.

entries.name: table.sort
entries.summary: Sorts an array in place; comp(a, b) returns true when a should come first.
entries.example: table.sort(scores, function(a, b) return a.points > b.points end)

entries.name: table.unpack
entries.summary: The elements of an array as separate values.

entries.name: table.pack
entries.summary: A table of the arguments with field n = their count.

entries.name: table.move
entries.summary: Copies elements a1[f..e] to a2[t..] (a2 defaults to a1).

entries.name: math
entries.summary: Mathematical functions and constants.
entries.description: Integers and floats are distinct subtypes; // is integer division, % is modulo, ^ is power (float). Hazard3 has no FPU, so integer arithmetic is much faster than float on the device.

entries.name: math.floor
entries.summary: The largest integer <= x (returns an integer).

entries.name: math.ceil
entries.summary: The smallest integer >= x.

entries.name: math.abs
entries.summary: Absolute value.

entries.name: math.max
entries.summary: The largest argument.

entries.name: math.min
entries.summary: The smallest argument.

entries.name: math.random
entries.summary: A random float in [0,1), integer in [1,m], or integer in [m,n].

entries.name: math.randomseed
entries.summary: Seeds the generator (seed from TimeNow() for variety).

entries.name: math.sqrt
entries.summary: Square root.

entries.name: math.fmod
entries.summary: Remainder of x / y with the sign of x.

entries.name: math.modf
entries.summary: Integral and fractional parts of x.

entries.name: math.tointeger
entries.summary: x as an integer when it has an exact integer value, else nil.

entries.name: math.type
entries.summary: "integer", "float" or nil for non-numbers.

entries.name: math.ult
entries.summary: Unsigned less-than comparison of integers.

entries.name: math.huge
entries.summary: Positive infinity.

entries.name: math.maxinteger
entries.summary: The largest integer (2^63-1, or 2^31-1 on a 32-bit build).

entries.name: math.mininteger
entries.summary: The smallest integer.

entries.name: math.sin
entries.summary: Sine (radians).

entries.name: math.cos
entries.summary: Cosine (radians).

entries.name: math.tan
entries.summary: Tangent.

entries.name: math.asin
entries.summary: Arc sine.

entries.name: math.acos
entries.summary: Arc cosine.

entries.name: math.atan
entries.summary: Arc tangent of y/x (two-argument form handles quadrants).

entries.name: math.exp
entries.summary: e^x.

entries.name: math.log
entries.summary: Natural logarithm, or in the given base.

entries.name: math.deg
entries.summary: Radians to degrees.

entries.name: math.rad
entries.summary: Degrees to radians.

entries.name: coroutine
entries.summary: Cooperative threads: functions that can pause (yield) and be resumed.
entries.description: Useful for scripted sequences inside tick(): resume the coroutine once per tick and yield between steps.

entries.name: coroutine.create
entries.summary: A new coroutine running f when first resumed.
entries.example:
local co = coroutine.create(function()
    Screen.OutLine("step 1") coroutine.yield()
    Screen.OutLine("step 2")
end)

entries.name: coroutine.resume
entries.summary: Runs the coroutine until it yields or ends.
entries.returns: true, yielded values... or false, err
entries.example: function tick() if coroutine.status(co) ~= "dead" then coroutine.resume(co) end end

entries.name: coroutine.yield
entries.summary: Pauses the running coroutine, passing values back to resume.

entries.name: coroutine.status
entries.summary: "running", "suspended", "normal" or "dead".

entries.name: coroutine.wrap
entries.summary: A function that resumes the coroutine each call (errors propagate).

entries.name: coroutine.running
entries.summary: The running coroutine and whether it is the main one.

entries.name: coroutine.isyieldable
entries.summary: True when the coroutine can yield.

entries.name: coroutine.close
entries.summary: Closes a suspended coroutine.

entries.name: utf8
entries.summary: UTF-8 helpers (the screen font is single-byte; these are for text data).

entries.name: utf8.char
entries.summary: A string from code points.

entries.name: utf8.codepoint
entries.summary: The code points of the characters at bytes i..j.

entries.name: utf8.codes
entries.summary: Iterates (position, code point) pairs.

entries.name: utf8.len
entries.summary: The number of characters (nil and the position on an invalid byte).

entries.name: utf8.offset
entries.summary: The byte position of the n-th character.

entries.name: utf8.charpattern
entries.summary: A pattern matching one UTF-8 character.

entries.name: package
entries.summary: The module system behind require().
entries.description: On the card, require's searcher looks for NAME.prg/.lua next to the program, at the root and in /lib. package.loaded caches loaded modules; package.preload can register modules from code.

entries.name: package.loaded
entries.summary: Modules already loaded, by name (require returns these without reloading).

entries.name: package.preload
entries.summary: Loader functions by module name, consulted by require before the card.
entries.example: package.preload["util"] = function() return { twice = function(n) return n * 2 end } end

entries.name: package.path
entries.summary: Lua's search path string (unused on the card: the fs searcher is in charge).
